title.narrative: Support to conflict displaced households’ emergency needs of food, NFI and sanitation/hygiene

description.narrative: The current conflict crises in South Sudan has made more than two million people to face severe insecurity; with famine narrowly avoided in 2014. But with the ongoing dry season the protracted conflict is only making the disaster worse, and unless more aid can be delivered to those who need it, mainly IDPs, – famine remains a serious threat in 2015. The Catholic Church and Caritas Yei in particular, have a mandate and commitment to assist the poor conflict-affected and vulnerable people. It does this, now, through a projects involving support to conflict and flood-affected populations in Kajo -Keji and Mundri Counties in Central and Western Equatoria states respectively. The conflict-affected persons, in Kajo Keji County, were as a result of cross border conflicts with neighbouring Madi tribe in Uganda. Whereas the conflicts in Mundri were of a dual nature; involving conflicts (between local famers and transhumant pastoralists from another state) and effect of floods. A total of 367 households are targeted. Of these 2,640 persons will be female and 180 males. Caritas Diocese of Yei (CDY) seeks to support these vulnerable people through provision of cash transfers to buy food and avert from the looming hunger. As the affected people have also lost homes and livelihood assets, especially for women, CDY will also provide the targeted beneficiaries with Non Food Items (NFIs) to meet their needs for basic shelter, clothing and access to household items. Given the conditions of congestion and poor sanitation/personal hygiene that the people are living in now, providing cash-for-food, NFIs distribution, latrines construction and hygiene awareness promotion to these households will positively impact on and alleviate their living conditions. Both men and women heads of households living in the camp will benefit from the project; with the host communities mainly benefiting from the hygiene awareness and promotion activities and earn incomes through the sale of their food produce to the IDPs. The project implementation, by CDY will be supported by the County RRC in Mundri-Western Equatoria state and the beneficiaries will also be involved in project implementation e.g. site designation and digging of pit latrines.
